verdict: READY TO MERGE - 16 of 16 findings resolved, 0 bubbled
strengths: test_prod_deploy_tracked.py is a real integration test: it builds a git repo with staged and untracked files and runs the unstubbed ProdCopier, covering folder files, top-level files, skipped reporting and the tracked_only=False path.
test_run_args.py parametrizes every documented version form from the _get_args docstring, plus duplicate, conflicting, unknown-flag and empty-prompt cases with their exit codes.

test_run_exit_code.py drives run.py through runpy as __main__, so the `raise SystemExit(main())` exit-code mapping is exercised end to end; its fakes replace collaborators only and the assertions check exit code and output, not stub calls.

_tracked_paths uses `git ls-files -z` with -C, so paths are unquoted, relative to source_root, and correct when source_root is a subdirectory of the repo; the docstring states the index semantics exactly.
The git lookup fails closed: a missing git binary (OSError) or a non-repo source (RuntimeError) becomes a CopyResult error before clean_dest can rmtree anything.
_scope_tracked re-roots the tracked set per folder and passes None through, so the tracked_only=False path stays byte-identical to the old walk.
Untracked files are reported in skipped instead of being dropped silently, and top-level files go through the same tracked filter.
run.py now returns explicit exit codes (0/1/2) through main() and SystemExit instead of relying on assert, which the -O flag would have stripped.
Argument parsing is split into _get_args and _resolve_version with docstrings that match argparse behavior, including the conflict and empty-prompt exits.
The git query runs before the clean_dest rmtree, so a missing git or a non-repository source fails without deleting the existing destination.
`git ls-files -z` with split on NUL avoids core.quotePath escaping, so non-ASCII and space-containing paths match the filesystem walk.
test_prod_deploy_tracked.py is a real integration test: it builds a git repo in tmp_path, stages a subset of files, and asserts on what lands on disk. No mocks.
Replacing `assert result.ok` with an explicit return code plus `raise SystemExit(main())` means failures survive `python -O` and surface to callers as exit 1.
_resolve_version normalizes whitespace before detecting conflicts, so `v3.17.2 -v ' v3.17.2'` is accepted while two genuinely different versions exit 2.
fpm.json fixes the scripts denied pattern from `scripts/fpm/_tbx_staging/**`, which never matched because patterns are folder-relative, to `fpm/_tbx_staging/**`.

important.name: New tests do not import under plain `pytest`
important.summary:
All three new test files import `conversion.*`, but the repo has no conftest.py, pytest.ini, or pyproject pythonpath setting, and tests/ has no __init__.py. In the default prepend import mode pytest puts tests/ on sys.path, not the repo root, so a bare `pytest` fails with ModuleNotFoundError: conversion. Only `python -m pytest` from the repo root works, because that adds the cwd. pytest is also missing from [dev-packages], so a fresh `pipenv install --dev` cannot run the suite at all.

Also (roast): The Pipfile adds `referencing` and `jsonschema` as runtime packages. Nothing in the repo imports either one: validation goes through pydantic's ProdConfig. Two unused dependencies to install and lock.
fix: Add an empty repo-root conftest.py (rootdir conftest puts the root on sys.path), or a pytest.ini / pyproject [tool.pytest.ini_options] with `pythonpath = .`; and add `pytest = "*"` under [dev-packages] in Pipfile.
Remove both lines from [packages].
If JSON-schema validation of project definitions is planned, land the code that uses them in the same change.

important.name: Repo-root discovery crashes in a git worktree or submodule
important.summary:
_get_repo_root matches any ancestor holding an entry named .git, then calls _is_git_folder on it. In a linked worktree or a submodule, .git is a file (gitdir: ...), so folder.exists() is True and folder.iterdir() raises NotADirectoryError. main() calls _bootstrap_sys_path unconditionally, so run.py dies with a traceback before any copy whenever it runs from a worktree, which is the normal workflow for this project. A freshly initialised repo with no .git/index also fails the superset check and walks on to a wrong or missing root. The search is not needed anyway: run.py always sits one level below the repo root.

Also (roast): _get_repo_root (run.py:20-31) finds '.git' via _search_down_for, then calls _is_git_folder, which runs folder.iterdir() on it. In a linked worktree '.git' is a file ('gitdir: ...'), so iterdir raises NotADirectoryError (WinError 267) and run.py dies before it parses anything useful. This project's workflow creates worktrees as standard practice, and tests/test_run_exit_code.py goes through the same path via runpy, so those tests fail when the suite runs from a worktree. It is a lot of repo detection for a file whose parent directory is already known: prod_deploy.py:26-27 finds its root with Path(__file__).parent.

Also (runtime): print(f'Parent: {parent.name}') runs for every ancestor on every invocation, so each run starts with noise lines ('Parent: conversion', 'Parent: Production_Convert') ahead of the real output. This is debug output left in the code.

Also (roast): run.py:25 prints 'Parent: <name>' for every directory it walks, on every run and in every test that goes through main(). That is debug output left in. Path(__file__) at line 21 is always truthy, so the `or Path().cwd()` fallback can never run. Line 39 raises FileExistsError for a folder that does not exist. Line 34 re-imports sys inside the function. Line 40 puts conversion/ itself on sys.path, so its modules can also be imported as top-level `prod_deploy`/`project_model`, a second identity nobody asked for. The `# Preview` comment at line 104 sits above a dry_run=False call. Each main() call in the tests also prepends two more sys.path entries.
fix: Replace the ancestor search with a fixed anchor: repo_root = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1], and drop _get_repo_root, _search_down_for, _is_git_folder and _GIT_FOLDER_CONTENTS.
Keep the search but accept .git as either a directory or a file: return parent as soon as (parent / '.git').exists(), and remove the iterdir-based content check.
Replace _get_repo_root, _is_git_folder and _search_down_for with `Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]`, which is the layout prod_deploy.py already assumes.
Keep the search but accept a '.git' file as well as a directory: return the first parent where `(parent / '.git').exists()`, and never iterdir a non-directory.
Delete the print call at conversion/run.py:25.

Delete the print at line 25 and the `or Path().cwd()` fallback, raise FileNotFoundError at line 39, drop the inner `import sys`, insert only the repo root into sys.path (once, if it is not already there), and remove or correct the `# Preview` comment.

important.name: Suite imports `conversion` with no rootdir/pythonpath configuration
important.summary: All three test modules import the `conversion` package by absolute name (`from conversion import run`, `from conversion.project_model import ...`, `import conversion.prod_deploy`). The repo has no conftest.py, pyproject.toml, pytest.ini or setup.cfg, and tests/ has no __init__.py, so pytest's default prepend import mode puts only tests/ on sys.path. A plain `pytest` invocation (the console script, where sys.path[0] is the Scripts dir, not the cwd) fails collection with ModuleNotFoundError: conversion; only `python -m pytest` from the repo root works, because it adds the cwd. The suite's pass/fail therefore depends on how it is launched.
fix: Add a repo-root pyproject.toml (or pytest.ini) with `[tool.pytest.ini_options] pythonpath = ["."]` and `testpaths = ["tests"]`.
Add an empty repo-root conftest.py so pytest's rootdir insertion puts the repo root on sys.path.

minor.name: Stale module docstring in prod_deploy.py
minor.summary: The module docstring names the directory `project_definition/` (lines 5, 81) and says it is 'next to this file'. The code uses `project_definitions`, one level up (_PROJECT_DEF_DIR = _HERE_DIR.parent / 'project_definitions'). The usage example `load_project("fbs")` (line 10) omits target_version, which is required, so it raises TypeError. Neither docstring mentions that the copy now requires git and a repository SOURCE_ROOT by default.
fix: Change lines 5 and 81-82 to `project_definitions/ (sibling of conversion/)`, change the usage example to `load_project("fpm", "v3.17.2")`, and add one line noting that tracked_only (default True) requires git on PATH.

minor.name: tracked_only ships uncommitted edits under a release version label
minor.summary: _tracked_paths filters on which paths are tracked, but _copy_file copies the working-tree bytes. A tracked file with uncommitted local edits (or a staged-only new file) goes into FPM_<version> as if it were the release. The version argument suggests a tagged build; the code does not check that the source tree is at that tag or clean. The filter answers 'is it tracked', not 'is this the committed release'.
fix: Before copying, run `git -C <source_root> status --porcelain -- <folders>`; return an error (or at least a warning in CopyResult) when the tree is dirty.
Export from the commit instead of the working tree (`git archive <target_version>` or `git show <rev>:<path>`), so the version label means the tag.

minor.name: Copy errors printed twice, to stdout
minor.summary: _copy_folder already prints `ERROR: {err}` for each copy failure (prod_deploy.py:319). run.py:109-111 now prints every error again as `\tERROR: ...`, so each folder copy failure shows up twice. Version errors go to stderr (run.py:84,90) but copy failures go to stdout, so a caller that captures stderr misses the actual cause of exit code 1.
fix: Delete the print at prod_deploy.py:319 so the library reports through CopyResult only, and send run.py's ERROR lines and 'Failed.' to sys.stderr. The assertion in test_failed_copy_exits_1 then reads capsys err instead of out.

minor.name: Commit messages omit the default-on git tracking filter
minor.summary: ProdConfig.tracked_only defaults to True, so every project definition (fpm.json and prod_deploy.json) now needs git on PATH and a repository SOURCE_ROOT, and untracked files are silently moved to skipped. None of the commit messages in the range mention this; 25be106 calls it 'deployment code modularization'.
fix: Add a line to the PR description: copies are now limited to git-tracked files by default (tracked_only), and a non-repository source is an error.

minor.name: Dead fallback and an unbound name in _get_repo_root
minor.summary:
Path(__file__) or Path().cwd() never reaches cwd() because Path objects are always truthy. Path(__file__) is also not resolved, so a relative or symlinked __file__ yields a relative parent chain. If all_parents is empty, the final raise references parent before assignment and raises NameError instead of FileNotFoundError.

Also (runtime): A missing scripts folder raises FileExistsError, which means the opposite. The function also inserts conversion/ itself at the front of sys.path, so every module in it can be imported a second time as a top-level module (project_model vs conversion.project_model), and each main() call adds duplicate entries. The str annotation on scripts_folder is reassigned to a Path, and the local `import sys` repeats the module-level import.
fix: Use start_path = Path(__file__).resolve() and drop the `or Path().cwd()` branch; build the error message from start_path instead of the loop variable.
Moot if the anchor fix for the worktree finding replaces the function.
Raise FileNotFoundError(str(scripts_folder)), insert only the repo root (skip when already present), drop the inner `import sys`, and rename the Path variable (e.g. scripts_dir).

minor.name: CLI help names the wrong destination folder
minor.summary: The parser description says files go to prod_results/FPM_<version>. The destination is DEST_ROOT from fpm.env, and the folder name comes from _generate_project_version_folder_name, which strips 'v' and turns dots into underscores: v3.17.2 lands in FPM_3_17_2, not FPM_v3.17.2.
fix: Change the description to 'Copy the fpm production files into <DEST_ROOT>/FPM_<version with dots as underscores>, e.g. FPM_3_17_2.'

minor.name: Version prompt crashes on EOF instead of exiting 2
minor.summary: The _resolve_version docstring says an empty answer exits with status 2. When stdin is closed or not interactive (scheduled task, piped run), input() raises EOFError and the run ends in a traceback with status 1, not the documented usage exit.
fix: Wrap the input() call in try/except EOFError, treat it as an empty answer (print 'No target version given.' to stderr and raise SystemExit(2)), and mention EOF in the docstring.

minor.name: '# Preview' comment above a real copy; errors print twice to stdout
minor.summary: main() labels ProdCopier(..., dry_run=False).run() as '# Preview', but it is a real write. Copy errors are now printed twice: once by ProdCopier._copy_folder (prod_deploy.py:319) and again by main's ERROR loop. Both go to stdout, while _resolve_version reports its failures on stderr.
fix: Delete or reword the '# Preview' comment, send main's ERROR lines and 'Failed.' to sys.stderr, and drop the print in _copy_folder so main is the only reporter (tests/test_run_exit_code.py reads capsys out, so update that assertion to err).

minor.name: reference/ no longer denies reference_modules and toolbox_figures
minor.summary: fpm.json drops `reference_modules/**` and `toolbox_figures/**` from the reference folder's denied list, and that folder has `allowed: []` (allow everything). Any tracked file under those two directories now ships to prod. The scripts folder's dropped patterns (_pre_tbx, _admin_utils, pyt_scripts) are harmless because `allowed: ["fpm/**"]` already excludes them. The reference ones are not covered by anything.
fix: Re-add `reference_modules/**` and `toolbox_figures/**` to reference.denied if they should stay out of prod.
If shipping them is intended, say so in the PR description.

minor.name: Non-git error test depends on tmp_path sitting outside any git repo and on git being installed
minor.summary:
test_non_git_source_is_an_error assumes `git -C <tmp_path>/plain ls-files` fails. If the pytest basetemp lies inside a repository (custom --basetemp under the project, a home/Temp tree under version control) or GIT_DIR/GIT_WORK_TREE are set in the environment (e.g. running from a git hook), ls-files succeeds, the run proceeds and the only error is `debug_override_rel not found in dest`, so the `git ls-files` assertion fails. If git is absent, the OSError text (`[WinError 2] ...`) does not contain `git ls-files` either, and every test in the module errors in `_git` instead of skipping.

Also (tests): _tracked_paths relies on `git -C <source_root> ls-files` printing paths relative to source_root, and _copy_top_level compares bare file names against that set. The fixture always makes source_root the repo root, so a regression to repo-root-relative paths (e.g. adding `--full-name` or running from the toplevel) would pass every test while shipping nothing when SOURCE_ROOT is nested.
fix: Add an autouse fixture that sets `GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES` to str(tmp_path) and deletes `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_WORK_TREE` via monkeypatch, and mark the module with `pytest.mark.skipif(shutil.which("git") is None, reason="git not installed")`.

Add a test that runs `git init` in tmp_path, builds the source tree under tmp_path/"src", stages the files from the repo root, and asserts the same shipped/skipped sets with ProjectPaths(tmp_path/"src", dst).

minor.name: Constant-absence test is a change detector; the version-to-load_project flow is untested
minor.summary: test_target_version_constant_removed asserts only that `run.TARGET_VERSION` no longer exists, which pins a removed implementation detail and would still pass if main() ignored the resolved version. No test checks that the parsed or prompted version actually reaches load_project: the fake in test_run_exit_code.py discards its `version` argument.
fix: Replace the hasattr test with a behavioral one: in test_run_exit_code.py let the fake load_project capture its arguments, run with `sys.argv = [RUN_PY, "v1.2.3"]`, and assert the captured version is "v1.2.3" (and that input() is not called).

minor.name: Fake copier result is class state mutated without teardown
minor.summary: Both tests assign `fake_copy.result = ...`, which writes the class attribute of the module-level _FakeCopier and survives the test. test_successful_copy_exits_0 only passes in isolation because it resets the value itself; any future test that uses the fixture without setting `result` inherits whatever the previous test left (e.g. the failing result), making outcomes order-dependent.
fix: In the fixture, build a fresh subclass per test (`copier = type("Copier", (_FakeCopier,), {"result": CopyResult((), (), (), ())})`) and patch ProdCopier with it.
Or set the attribute through `monkeypatch.setattr(_FakeCopier, "result", ...)` so it is restored at teardown.

minor.name: runpy of run.py leaks sys.path edits into the rest of the session
minor.summary: Each runpy.run_path call executes main(), which calls _bootstrap_sys_path() and inserts both the repo root and the conversion/ folder at sys.path[0] with no cleanup. After these tests, bare module names under conversion/ (e.g. `project_model`, `prod_deploy`, `run`) shadow anything of the same name for every later test, and the entries accumulate once per call. The fixture restores argv, input, load_project and ProdCopier but not sys.path.
fix: In the fake_copy fixture add `monkeypatch.setattr(sys, "path", list(sys.path))` so the inserted entries are discarded at teardown.
